title: SAML federation rollback & KMS escrow validation — signoff checklist and gating PRD
creator: Emily Chen
description: Define acceptance gates and a prescriptive sign-off checklist for two related operational risks in Private deployments: (1) automated and manual rollback of SAML/SAML-F federation configurations under failure or compromise scenarios, and (2) validation of KMS/HSM escrow and recovery procedures prior to customer handoff. The goal is to ensure safe rollback without losing auditability, to validate dual-control KMS escrow proofs, and to tie the checks into onboarding and upgrade gates.
scope: Authn/authz: SAML identity provider (IdP) configuration rollback workflow for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem).
KMS escrow: verification steps for customer key escrow artifacts, HSM operator procedures, and remote/airgapped recovery playbooks.
Audit: retention and tamper-evidence checks for SSO configuration changes and KMS escrow operations.
Sign-off: checklist for PM/SEC/OPS/SRE to greenlight customer onboarding or major SSO/KMS change rollout.
out_of_scope: Implementing new KMS vendor integrations (separate PRD).
Changes to hosted API SSO flows (hosted API is out of scope).
Automated key rotation tooling (only validation & acceptance of rotation procedures).
requirements: 1) Rollback plan must preserve last-known-good SAML metadata and be executable within a documented maintenance window.
2) Every rollback action must generate an immutable audit record (who, when, what, reason) stored for minimum 365 days and exportable to customer audit package.
3) KMS escrow validation must include dual-control release simulation (two independent operator approvals) and proof artifacts (signed release manifest + HSM attestation).
4) Onboarding gate requires a dry-run of escrow restore in a sandbox environment with noise-level and latency metrics recorded.
5) If rollback is triggered by suspected compromise, system must support an emergency key rotation path with documented operator steps and rollback abortion instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Engineering runbook for SAML rollback exists, reviewed by Security, and validated in a staged cluster (logs and timeline attached).
AC-2: KMS escrow restore dry-run completed against sandbox instance; artifacts (release manifest, operator signatures, HSM attestation) uploaded to Confluence and verified by PM and SecOps.
AC-3: Audit pipeline captures rollback events with WORM (write-once) retention and can produce a customer-facing evidence bundle within 48 hours.
AC-4: Automated smoke tests detect regressions after rollback and report to the Console dashboard; alerts configured and exercised during dry-run.
AC-5: Stakeholder signoff recorded from Security, SRE, and Customer Onboarding before production rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize runbooks, acceptance checklist, and test matrix — (owner: PM).
Phase 1 (Staging dry-runs): execute SAML rollback and KMS restore in staging; capture artifacts; triage failures — (owner: Eng).
Phase 2 (Canary): perform controlled rollback/restore in single-customer dedicated environment with monitoring and on-call present — (owner: SRE).
Phase 3 (Production gating): require signoff checklist completed and Security approval to enable feature for broader onboarding — (owner: PM + Security).
signoff_checklist: Checklist: Runbook published and link included in ticket.
Checklist: Staging dry-run artifacts attached (signed manifest, HSM attestation, logs).
Checklist: Audit export validated and customer evidence package generated successfully.
Checklist: SRE incident playbook updated with rollback/restore runbook references.
Checklist: Security review completed and issues remediated (CVE, misconfig findings).
Checklist: Customer onboarding team trained on abort and escalation flows.
Checklist: Legal/compliance signoff where required for specific customers (e.g., regulated verticals).
work_log: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Emily Chen. Initial scope and goals captured. Linked to PM-12587 and PM-47280 for upstream compliance context.
2025-02-14: Design sync with Eng (Raj Patel) and Security (Maya Ruiz). Decided to require dual-control operator signatures for all escrow releases.
2025-02-21: Eng spike completed (ENG-1982). Found that current audit pipeline lacks WORM export for SAML metadata changes — created ENG-2765.
2025-02-24: Dry-run scheduled for 2025-03-03 in staging; Onboarding team to observe. PRD updated with test matrix.
2025-03-03: Dry-run executed; one failure in HSM attestation collection (race during key material handoff). Root cause logged and remediation in progress. Artifacts partially uploaded.
2025-03-04: Security review meeting — added two additional acceptance tests for emergency key rotation. Updated acceptance criteria and extended due_date to 2025-03-14.
notes: Decision: prefer manual operator approval for first two months post-launch; revisit automation after 2 successful canaries.
Trade-off: requiring dual-control slows emergency restores by ~15 minutes but significantly reduces blast radius for accidental releases.
Follow-up: schedule a 90-day post-launch runbook audit; add this ticket to quarterly security playbook review.
Customer communication: onboarding letter template drafted to explain rollback and evidence package access for customers requiring audit artifacts.
